source_text:
Ταῦτα, ἀγαπητοί, οὐ μόνον ὑμᾶς νουθετοῦντες ἐπιστέλλομεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἑαυτοὺς ὑπομιμνήσκοντες: ἐν γὰρ τῷ αὐτῷ ἐσμὲν σκάμματι, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς ἡμῖν ἀγὼν ἐπίκειται.
διὸ ἀπολίπωμεν τὰς κενὰς καὶ ματαίας φροντίδας, καὶ ἔλθωμεν ἐπὶ τὸν εὐκλεῆ καὶ σεμνὸν τῆς παραδόσεως ἡμῶν κανόνα,
καὶ ἴδωμεν, τί καλὸν καὶ τί τερπνὸν καὶ τί προσδεκτὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
ἀτενίσωμεν εἰς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ γνῶμεν, ὡς ἔστιν τίμιον τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν ἐκχυθὲν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ μετανοίας χάριν ὑπήνεγκεν.
διέλθωμεν εἰς τὰς γενεὰς πάσας, καὶ καταμάθωμεν ὅτι ἐν γενεᾷ καὶ γενεᾷ μετανοίας τόπον ἔδωκεν ὀ δεσπότης τοῖς βουλομένοις ἐπιστραφῆναι ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
Νῶε ἐκήρυξεν μετάνοιαν, καὶ οἱ ὑπακούσαντες ἐσώθησαν.
Ἰωνᾶς Νινευΐταις καταστροφὴν ἐκήρυξεν: οἱ δὲ μετανοήσαντες ἐπὶ τοῖς ἁμαρτήμασιν αὐτῶν ἐξιλάσαντο τὸν θεὸν ἱκετεύσαντες καὶ ἔλαβον σωτηρίαν, καίπερ ἀλλότριοι τοῦ θεοῦ ὄντες.
thought_title: Repentance as the Path Back to God
orientation: The Roman church, writing to the Corinthians, has just shown how envy and faction destroyed great cities and nations, and now turns to exhortation, urging the Corinthians to abandon empty cares and return to the rule of tradition, looking to Christ's blood and the examples of Noah and Jonah as proof that God gives a place of repentance in every generation.
pass_a_gloss: These things, beloved, not only admonishing you we write, but also ourselves reminding: for in the same we are arena, and the same for us contest lies upon. Therefore let us leave behind the empty and vain cares, and let us come to the glorious and reverend of our tradition rule, and let us see, what good and what pleasing and what acceptable before the one who made us. Let us gaze at the blood of Christ and let us know, how it is precious to his Father, because for our salvation poured out for all the world grace of repentance it brought. Let us go through all the generations, and let us learn that in generation and generation a place of repentance gave the Master to those willing to turn back to him. Noah preached repentance, and those who obeyed were saved. Jonah to the Ninevites destruction preached: but those who repented over their sins propitiated God by supplicating and received salvation, although strangers of God being.

lemmas.gloss: arena, the dug-out place for athletic contests

choices.why: The athletic metaphor of a dug-out wrestling pit fits the following word 'contest' and the letter's agonistic imagery; 'arena' preserves the concrete image.
Continues the athletic metaphor; 'contest' keeps the sense of a shared struggle rather than a military battle.
The pair describes the rule of tradition as both renowned and solemn; 'reverend' captures the dignity and awe due to the inherited order.
The verb means fixed, intense looking; 'gaze' conveys the sustained attention the author calls for.
The genitive phrase means the gift or favor that is repentance; 'grace of repentance' keeps the theological weight of χάρις as unmerited gift.
The verb means to appease or make favorable, especially God; 'propitiated' preserves the cultic sense of turning away divine wrath.

pass_b_english: We are writing these things to you, beloved, not only to admonish you but also to remind ourselves. For we are in the same arena, and the same contest lies before us.
So let us abandon empty and vain cares, and let us come to the glorious and venerable rule of our tradition. Let us see what is good and pleasing and acceptable in the sight of the one who made us.
Let us gaze at the blood of Christ and know how precious it is to his Father. It was poured out for our salvation, and it brought the grace of repentance to the whole world.
Let us go through all the generations and learn thoroughly that in generation after generation the Master has given a place of repentance to those who wish to turn back to him.
Noah preached repentance, and those who obeyed were saved.
Jonah preached destruction to the Ninevites. But they repented of their sins, propitiated God by their supplications, and received salvation, even though they were strangers to God.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer units; made the subject of each action explicit; clarified the sequence of ideas about Christ's blood and repentance; kept all claims and Scripture references intact.
Clarified the rule of tradition as venerable rather than reverend, kept Master consistently for God, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

notes.quote: the glorious and reverend rule of our tradition

variants.text: the glorious and reverend rule of our tradition

notes.why: 'Reverend rule' is odd; likely means 'venerable tradition' or 'way of life'.
